finding.title: Chunk pushLedgerEntriesBatch at the 500-op WriteBatch limit like pushCompletionsBatch — it currently commits every entry in one unbounded batch

finding.why: pushCompletionsBatch (lines 245-285) correctly loops in <=500-item chunks via _writeBatchLimit and catches per-chunk failures into SyncPushException(committed:...). Its sibling pushLedgerEntriesBatch (lines 454-472), the batch entry point for the outbox's learning_ledger kind, instead puts every caller-supplied entry into a single _firestore.batch() and calls .commit() once with no chunk loop and no try/catch. grep across lib/ finds zero callers today (PushPipeline's and SyncOrchestrator's test fakes both stub it as an unused no-op), so it isn't live yet, but it IS unit-tested in this file as if production-ready (max 3 entries tested), and fake_cloud_firestore's own MockWriteBatch enforces the identical 500-task cap real Firestore does. The first caller who batches >500 pending ledger entries gets an unhandled 'Firestore supports at most 500 tasks in a batch' exception with zero partial-commit accounting, not the graceful per-chunk degrade FB-5 requires — and every retry of that same backlog fails identically, wedging that user's ledger sync.
finding.recommendation: Give pushLedgerEntriesBatch the same chunk loop, per-chunk try/catch, and SyncPushException(committed:) accounting as pushCompletionsBatch (ideally factor both into a shared chunking helper); add a >500-entry test mirroring the one recommended for pushCompletionsBatch below.
acceptance_criteria: pushLedgerEntriesBatch splits entries into <=500-item WriteBatch chunks and reports partial commits on mid-drain failure, matching pushCompletionsBatch's contract
New test pushes >500 ledger entries through the real method with an injected chunk-2 failure and asserts on committed/failed accounting
